paragraphs.text: A file-upload plugin for the DeepSeek Harness.
# dsh-web-file-uploader
> **🌐 Language** · English | 中文（简体）
This is a file-upload plugin developed for DeepSeek Harness. It adds a DeepSeek Web Chat style **pap
erclip attach button** to the prompt input field, uploads the selected files to the **DSH host machi
ne**, and applies **model-aware adaptation** so the files are actually readable by the running model
; it also supports **content-addressed deduplication**.
It currently supports web and desktop; support for dsh-TUI is planned.
If you want to see the plugin's running effects, see in Gallary.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Recently, because my npm account is still being recovered, I am unable to publish p
ackages. If a package with the same name suddenly appears on npm, please do not download or install

it!
>
> For distribution sources not supported by this project, use them at your own risk! Please re
port any security issues related to distribution sources in Issues.
## Features
- 📎 Paperclip button in the composer tool row: its style basically matches the button inside DeepSee

k Web Chat, with the paperclip rotated 45° to distinguish it from the official built-in feature.
- T
he official upload entry can be **replaced**: the shell's "Add → File" row (shared by the `+` menu a
nd the `/` slash menu) is swapped in place for this plugin's own entry — same "File" text, but the i
con uses this plugin's own angled paperclip and the command becomes `attach-file`. The standalone co
mposer button stays visible by default and can be hidden while the replacement is on, letting the me

nu entry be the only upload control.
- Multi-file selection; each file is shown as a **preview-style
attachment card** above the composer (images show a thumbnail): reading → uploading → saved, with c
opy-path and remove actions, plus a permanent delete button that appears only when a new stored copy

was created (that action really deletes the file from disk).
- Once a real upload creates a new cop
y, it is stored on the DSH host in a directory managed by the plugin, and collected automatically by

GC (garbage collection).
- Filenames are sanitized automatically (path separators, `..`, control ch
aracters rejected), and `-1`/`-2` suffixes are appended for files with the same name but different c

ontent.
- **Content-addressed deduplication**: a repeated file is referenced directly instead of bei

ng uploaded again.
- UI strings localized through the app's `locale` service (zh/en; follows the dsh
web language setting or the system default)
## Usage
> This assumes you have just installed the plugin and have not changed any default setting. The plug
in's settings page documents every option in detail if you want to look into them.
Click the angled paperclip button in the prompt input field and the system file picker opens; choose
the files you need and confirm.
After uploading, each file is shown as a card above the prompt input field where you can adjust it.
Once you press send, the cards still present are turned into file paths and injected into the text p
rompt, appended to the end of the user message for the model to read and analyse. Read on for more t
o the end of the user message for the model to read and analyse. Read on for more technical details.
To install this plugin right away, jump to Installation.
## File storage location
An uploaded file copy lands in `$DSH_HOME/uploads` (default `~/.dsh/uploads`) on the DSH host.
The deduplication index (`uploads/.dfu-index.json`) lives in the same directory as the stored files.
## Model-aware adaptation & the attachment-card design
Uploaded files are shown as **attachment cards** in the dock above the composer. The cards are the s
ource of truth for injection:
| State | Behavior |
| Card present | The file's absolute path is injected into **the user messages about to be sent**. |
| Card closed (`×`) | The file card disappears, and the uploaded copy is **kept on disk** and track

ed by the plugin. |
| Card deleted (🗑) | The file card disappears, the uploaded copy is **permanentl

y removed from the DSH host**, and the tracking index is updated accordingly. |
| Ctrl+V paste | Pas
ted images ride the native draft pipeline; the plugin does not interfere |
The distinction between `×` and 🗑 is intentional: `×` just stops injecting (you might want the model
to find the file later), while 🗑 is a statement that you are **done with the file forever**. When t
he last reference is deleted, the file is removed from disk if it lives in the plugin-managed direct
ory; if another live session still references the same deduplicated copy, the file is kept and only
this session's reference is dropped.
A re-upload hits deduplication and reuses the same stored path, so such a card merely **borrows** an
existing copy rather than owning it. Those cards do not show 🗑, because deleting permanently from h
ere would also remove a file other references still use, so they keep only `×` to release the refere
nce; for file-level deletion use the plugin's settings page, where the "in use" rule also protects f
iles referenced by live sessions.
This is a deliberate design decision: a card **does not disappear automatically** after sending (unl
ike paste previews that clear on send), so you decide how long a file stays "attached" to the conver
sation. Each injection is one-shot (one per message), and the injected block lists exactly the files
of all currently **open** cards.
Injection is distinguished by model capability:
| Model type | Image files (png/jpeg/webp/gif) | Other files |
[该节后续省略]
### Compatibility with vision-tools and other plugins
- **Zero coupling**: the plugin only injects absolute paths into the prompt; it never calls, wraps,
or assumes any auxiliary tool, and a tool such as vision-tools or a similar image-reading tool simpl

y works independently once it has the path.
- **Native multimodal path**: for image-capable models,
images are injected as native `ImageBlock`s, and the model can read and recognise them with its own

multimodal ability.
- **Non-invasive**: injection targets only real user messages; steering / system
messages are never injected, and a message that already carries the `[Attached files]` marker is ne
ver injected twice. Pasting images via Ctrl+V is handled entirely by the product's native pipeline.
## Architecture
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The browser never holds the bytes as base64: the `File` itself is the request body, and the host str
eams it to a staging file while hashing the same pass.
